cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is a prisoner on his way to Rome. His ship wrecked, but everyone on board made it safely to land on the island of Malta (Acts 27:44; 28:1). Now it's time to get back on the water.

cards.question: How long do Paul and the others stay on Malta before they set sail again?

cards.text: They board an Alexandrian ship that spent the winter at the island, with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead. After one shipwreck, friend, I'm checking that boat for leaks BEFORE I sit down.

Three days at Syracuse, a stop at Rhegium, then a south wind comes up, and they reach Puteoli, where they find some brothers, fellow believers in Jesus. That's more stops than my morning commute, and I LIVE in my bakery.

cards.question: Paul and his group step off the ship in Puteoli and meet the brothers there. What do the brothers do?

answers.text: Invite the group to stay with them
Send the group straight on to Rome
Report the group to the soldiers

cards.question: After the stay in Puteoli, Paul's journey keeps going, and so they come to ___.

cards.text: Believers in Rome who heard about them travel as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet them. When my drawer opened, people were looking for tape, not me.

cards.question: When Paul sees the believers from Rome who came out to meet him, he is encouraged and gives thanks to God.

cards.text: When they finally arrive in Rome, Paul's still a prisoner. All those miles, all that water, and the man STILL doesn't get to pick where he sleeps.

cards.question: Where does the prisoner Paul get to stay in Rome?

answers.text: By himself with a soldier to guard him
In the city prison with other prisoners
In the house of a Roman official

cards.text: After three days, Paul calls together the leaders of the Jews in Rome. Once they've gathered, he speaks to them as brothers.

cards.question: Paul admits to the leaders that he has done something against their people and the customs of their fathers.

cards.text: Even so, Paul says, he was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans. They examined him and found no basis for a death sentence.

cards.question: After examining Paul, what did the Romans want to do with him?

answers.text: Keep him in chains for life

cards.text: But when the Jews objected, Paul was compelled to appeal to Caesar, the Roman emperor. That's like your manager saying you're good to go, then somebody complains, and now you're on a flight to corporate HEADQUARTERS.

cards.question: Paul tells the leaders he came to Rome to bring a charge against his own nation.
Paul is bound with a chain. What reason does he give the leaders for it?

answers.text: Because of the hope of Israel
Because he broke a Roman law

cards.text: The leaders say no letters about Paul came from Judea, and none of the brothers from there reported or mentioned anything bad about him. I bet Paul walked in braced for drama, and the group chat was DEAD quiet.

cards.question: What do the Jewish leaders in Rome tell Paul they want from him?
The Jewish leaders tell Paul that the sect he's part of, the followers of Jesus, is welcomed by people everywhere.

cards.text: They set a day, many people come to where Paul's staying, and he teaches from morning to evening about the kingdom of God and about Jesus. Morning to EVENING, and I can't go ten minutes without checking my oven.

cards.question: To persuade the people about Jesus, what does Paul teach from?

answers.text: The Law of Moses and the Prophets
Letters from the church in Judea

cards.question: After a whole day of Paul's teaching, how do the people respond?

answers.text: Some are convinced and others refuse
Every one of them believes him
None of them will listen at all

cards.text: They disagree among themselves and start to leave after Paul makes a final statement. He says the Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to their fathers through Isaiah the prophet (Isaiah 6:9-10).
Here are those words: "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, this people hears and sees but never understands, because their ___ has grown callous.
Isaiah's words say that if this people would see, hear, understand and turn, they would be healed.

cards.text: Then Paul wraps up that final statement, and it's a BIG one. He tells them where God's salvation has been sent.

cards.question: Where does Paul say God's salvation has been sent?

answers.text: To the priests in the temple

cards.text: And Paul adds about the Gentiles, "and they will listen!" Isaiah spoke of people ever hearing but never understanding, and Paul says these folks WILL listen.
Paul stays two full years in his own rented house. I spent years in a junk drawer rent free, and trust me, friend, that is NOT the same thing.

cards.question: In his rented house in Rome, who does Paul welcome?

answers.text: All who come to visit him

cards.question: During those two years, Paul keeps quiet about Jesus to stay out of trouble.

cards.text: Here's how it ends: "Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ." The man's wearing a chain, and NOTHING could chain up that message.

findings.problem: The correct answer is the only grammatically possible option. "Hands" and "feet" are plural, so neither fits "their ___ has grown callous." This makes "heart" stand out and lets the baker answer from grammar rather than the passage's meaning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card cites only Acts 28:28, but its second sentence also retells Acts 28:26 when it says Isaiah spoke of people ever hearing but never understanding. That earlier verse is not covered by the card's citation or given its own reference.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The distractor "Those who agree with him" is not clearly false. Acts 28:24 says some people were convinced, and those people would be included among all the visitors Paul welcomed. Without a restriction such as "Only," a baker could argue that this answer is true but incomplete.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
